record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.context_brief: Complex environmental constraints in URM ARM
record.original_question: Adjacency constraints and maximum opening-size limits capture only part of the environmental planning problem, because managers also care about fragmentation, wildlife corridors, edge effects, and preserving balanced patches of mature forest. The open question is how to extend URM and ARM harvest-scheduling formulations to include these richer environmental constraints while keeping the models computationally tractable.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 How can we include complex environmental considerations like fragmentation, corridors, balancing mature patches, etc. into URM and ARM formulations in a computationally feasible way?

artifact.status_search_result: Several partial results exist. Recent works extend URM/ARM formulations to include mature-patch constraints (Rebain & McDill 2003; Carvajal et al. on mature-patch promotion), connectivity/corridor MIP constraints (Könnyű et al.), perimeter-minimization for compact patches, and an "Extended Unit Restriction Model with Environmental Considerations" (Forests, 2023). However, no single tractable formulation simultaneously captures fragmentation, corridors, edge effects, and balanced mature patches at realistic scales; the general problem remains an active research direction.

status_evidence.title: An Extended Unit Restriction Model with Environmental Considerations for Forest Harvesting
status_evidence.snippet: Forest harvesting problems with adjacency constraints can include additional environmental constraints to protect wildlife habitats...
status_evidence.claim: Recent extension of URM with environmental considerations exists but addresses only some of the listed concerns.

status_evidence.title: Promoting Large, Compact Mature Forest Patches in Harvest Scheduling Models
status_evidence.snippet: Formulations that extend these models by constraining or minimizing total perimeter of patches, producing solutions with fewer, larger, and more compact patches.
status_evidence.claim: Mature-patch and compactness constraints have been partially incorporated.

status_evidence.title: Can mature patch constraints mitigate the fragmenting effects of harvest opening size restrictions?
status_evidence.snippet: Mature patch constraints to mitigate fragmenting effects of harvest opening size restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial work on fragmentation mitigation in ARM-type models.

status_evidence.title: Imposing Connectivity Constraints in Forest Planning Models
status_evidence.snippet: MIP frameworks for corridor connection in spatially constrained harvest scheduling.
status_evidence.claim: Corridor/connectivity constraints have been formulated but tractability for combined constraints remains open.
